driver_narrative: Peak diurnal commuter rush (08:00-11:00 and 17:00-21:00) represents the dominant positive driver, lifting congestion by 12-18% above network baseline.
Prior 1-hour lag speed and 3-hour rolling average provide strong autoregressive anchoring, dampening or amplifying delays based on existing network saturation.
Physical road carriageway width (>6 lanes) acts as a structural congestion dampener (-3% to -8%), whereas high accident hazard index increases delay variance.
Precipitation (>5 mm/hr) and active rain flags consistently elevate congestion by 4-9% due to wet pavement friction and reduced speed thresholds.
Major festivals and assemblies (Durga Puja, Ganesh Visarjan, Diwali) introduce acute localized congestion spikes of +8% to +16% during scheduled assembly intervals.
